description: Use this when the user asks what research has found on a question in the biology of aging or an age-related disease, often without the word aging: senolytics, epigenetic clocks, partial reprogramming, mitochondria, NAD+, immune aging, ovarian aging and menopause, neurodegeneration, sarcopenia, long-lived species. Pass 2 to 4 key terms, not the question: "rapamycin lifespan humans", not "does rapamycin extend lifespan in humans". Searches the titles and abstracts of every paper AgingResearch.News has read, best match first, by default only papers about aging. Supports "quoted phrases", OR, -exclusions and the filters below. When the terms together find fewer than 3 papers, the results match all but one of them (relaxed: true). The record is not all of PubMed: no match does not mean no study exists. Not for personal medical advice, symptoms or product recommendations. Read one in full with get_paper.

age_link.description: How the work itself connects to aging.

author.description: Papers by an author. A name matches every author who answers to it: the words in any order, with or without accents, an initial standing for any name it begins (`sinclair d`). An `author_id` from a paper's `authors_full` (an OpenAlex author id such as `A5022713595`, or an ORCID iD) matches that one person.

category.description: Category slug. A paper matches when its category or its secondary category is listed.

cursor.description: From the last page's `pagination.next_cursor`; keep the other arguments the same.

min_relevance.description: How closely papers must bear on aging, 0 to 3. Leave out for papers about aging; 1 adds adjacent papers; 0 returns every paper read, most of them not about aging.

preprint.description: `true` for preprints only, `false` for peer-reviewed papers only. Omit for both.

q.description: Search terms: 2 to 4 key terms work best. Supports "quoted phrases", OR and -exclusions.

since.description: Only papers added on or after this UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD; a full ISO timestamp is cut to its date).

system.description: Body system key (see `systems`). A paper matches when it involves any of them. Only papers that have been analyzed have systems.

until.description: Only papers added on or before this UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD).

name: search_papers
